A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the residual interaction in a nucleus is a complicated function of its single-particle energies, which cannot be described in terms of a few phenomenological interaction parameters.
the residual interaction is determined by the conservation of the total momentum and of the total angular momentum, which are the only conserved quantities in nuclei.
the single-particle energies of a nucleus are determined by the nuclear mean field and by the residual interaction.
